title: The Growing Square Mystery
outcome: The student will explain why doubling the sides of a square quadruples its area because growth happens in two dimensions simultaneously.
subject: math

concepts.title: The Growing Square Mystery
concepts.centralCause: When both dimensions of a flat shape are multiplied by a factor k, the area increases by k squared because the shape grows in both length and width at once.
conditions: Both dimensions (length and width) must be scaled by the same factor
The thickness or coverage per unit remains constant

cards.title: Counting the Squares

fact.statement: Area is the number of unit squares needed to cover a shape's surface.
fact.source: OpenStax Prealgebra 2e, 9.4 Use Properties of Rectangles, Triangles, and Trapezoids (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/prealgebra-2e/pages/9-4-use-properties-of-rectangles-triangles-and-trapezoids

hook.question: If you have a 3x3 square made of 9 tiles, what happens if you double the length of every side?
hook.predictPrompt: Predict how many tiles you would need for the new shape and explain why.

cards.explanation: Area measures the surface space inside a boundary. Think of a square as a grid. A 3x3 square uses 9 small squares. When you double the sides to 6x6, you aren't just adding a row; you are adding rows and columns simultaneously. This creates a much larger space than just doubling the original count.

action.instruction: Take 9 sticky notes and arrange them in a 3x3 square. Imagine doubling the side length to 6. Predict how many notes you'd need to fill the new 6x6 area, then count how many fit in a 6x6 grid.

cards.title: The Two-Way Growth

fact.statement: Scaling a square's sides by a factor of k multiplies the area by k squared.
conditions: Both sides scaled by the same factor
fact.source: OpenStax Prealgebra 2e, 9.4 Use Properties of Rectangles, Triangles, and Trapezoids (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/prealgebra-2e/pages/9-4-use-properties-of-rectangles-triangles-and-trapezoids

hook.question: Why does a 6x6 square hold four times as much as a 3x3 square?
hook.predictPrompt: Predict what happens to the area if you triple the sides of a 3x3 square. Explain your reasoning.

cards.explanation: When you scale a square, you are stretching it in two directions: length and width. If you triple the sides, the length becomes 3 times longer AND the width becomes 3 times wider. The total area grows by 3 times 3, which is 9. This is why scaling is not a simple 1-to-1 increase.

action.instruction: Imagine a 3x3 square. In your mind, triple the side length to 9. Predict how many times larger the area becomes compared to the original 3x3, then think about how many 3x3 squares fit into a 9x9 square.

cards.title: The Rectangle Exception

fact.statement: If only one side of a rectangle is doubled, the area only doubles.
fact.source: OpenStax Prealgebra 2e, 9.4 Use Properties of Rectangles, Triangles, and Trapezoids (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/prealgebra-2e/pages/9-4-use-properties-of-rectangles-triangles-and-trapezoids

hook.question: What happens if you double the length of a rectangle but keep the width exactly the same?
hook.predictPrompt: Predict if the area will double, triple, or quadruple. Explain why.

cards.explanation: Area is length times width. If you only change one dimension, like the length, the width stays constant. Therefore, the area only grows by that single change. This is different from a square where both sides change at once. To double the area of a rectangle, you only need to double one side.

action.instruction: Imagine a rectangle that is 2 units wide and 3 units long. Imagine doubling only the length to 6 units while keeping the width at 2. Predict the new area, then calculate it.

acceptable: It doubled because only the length was doubled.

cards.title: Paint vs. Fences

fact.statement: Flat surfaces (paint, tiles) scale with area, while edges (fences, frames) scale with perimeter.
fact.source: OpenStax Prealgebra 2e, 9.4 Use Properties of Rectangles, Triangles, and Trapezoids (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/prealgebra-2e/pages/9-4-use-properties-of-rectangles-triangles-and-trapezoids

hook.question: If you double the sides of a square garden, do you need 2 times as much fence or 4 times as much grass seed?
hook.predictPrompt: Predict which one needs more and explain why.

cards.explanation: Perimeter is the distance around the outside (a line). Area is the space inside (a surface). When you double the sides of a square, the perimeter (the fence) only doubles because it's a 1D measurement. However, the area (the grass) quadruples because it grows in two directions. Paint and tiles also follow the area rule.

action.instruction: Imagine a square garden with a fence around it. If you double the side length, predict if the fence length doubles or quadruples. Then, think about the grass inside.

cards.title: The Master Architect

fact.statement: Scaling a 2D shape by factor k results in an area multiplied by k squared.
conditions: Both sides scaled by the same factor
fact.source: OpenStax Prealgebra 2e, 9.4 Use Properties of Rectangles, Triangles, and Trapezoids (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/prealgebra-2e/pages/9-4-use-properties-of-rectangles-triangles-and-trapezoids

hook.question: You are an architect designing a square plaza. If you want to make the plaza 5 times wider and 5 times longer, how many times larger will the area be?
hook.predictPrompt: Predict the multiplier for the area and explain the reason.

cards.explanation: Since the plaza is a flat shape, when you multiply both the length and the width by 5, the area grows by 5 times 5. This is because the growth happens in both directions simultaneously. The area is always the product of the two sides. If both sides are multiplied by 5, the total area is multiplied by 25.

action.instruction: Imagine a square plaza. If you multiply both sides by 5, predict how many times the area increases. Then, calculate the area of a 1x1 square and a 5x5 square to verify.
